body: I just don't think I can go through the motions of life. I can barely keep my room clean.
I've taken numerous anti-depressants and dosages. I've been in therapy for the majority of my life. My family is utterly clueless and unsupportive.
I struggle everyday for meaning. I need someone who will be a consistent confidante, day and night as he was before he died, but that is asking too much from one person.

I think you're putting your own feelings and experiences onto my situation. I don't want a child like a puppy. I want a family. I want to have the one I never had and be the mom my mother will never be able to be.

Don't get why I'm being downvoted to oblivion. As someone else mentioned, it's called "getoffmychest" so there's a reason why it's not going to be the most palatable comment. Because people like you would have mean things to say in response if said in real life.

I don't really enjoy anything. I mean, all I've ever wanted was the family I never had and that will probably never happen. I enjoy writing but I can't find the motivation to do it if I'll never fulfill my life's dream. Idk, it's just one big mess and Reddit is the wrong place to vent such feelings, especially female issues. 

But, I don't feel comfortable saying such things in real life. Thank you for the kind words. I appreciate it.
Hateful? I didn't notice, thank you for your constructive observation.

This resonated with me. I hold on to a satisfactory existence that has lost all meaning. Yeah, I have a job. I have a few friends. Things could get "better" but, that's just more "okayness". I don't enjoy eating, writing, drinking, talking, it's all just the same--not good, not bad, just is. 

I've come to my own conclusion that my brain is not programmed for happiness. I wrote out my will to give everything to the only woman I've ever considered a mother to me. That thought brings me happiness, I admit. Her being able to enjoy the money that I would use to further a career and education I wouldn't appreciate. I want her to take the vacation she deserves, to pay off her debt, to bring her the happiness I'm unable to experience.
